mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: wear reached an unported branch: Cloak_on() for otyp 139

summary: The first mismatch is the JavaScript wear path refusing an elven cloak before C’s Cloak_on() runs. In do_wear.c, the ELVEN_CLOAK arm calls toggle_stealth(); the saved C recording shows “You move very quietly.” at step 30. The later +6 enchantment evaporation belongs to read.c and remains a separate downstream behavior.

source.branch: Whole-function scope is do_wear.c:Cloak_on() (325-380): after an armor cloak has been set in uarmc, compute oldprop from its oc_oprop with WORN_CLOAK stripped, dispatch all 12 cloak-type cases (including ELVEN_CLOAK -> toggle_stealth), perform the final known/update_inventory handling, and retain the default impossible branch. The assigned C path reaches the ELVEN_CLOAK case when accessory_or_armor_on() has accepted the cloak, set W_ARMC, and invoked the zero-delay callback. toggle_stealth() reports/discovers stealth only when no other extrinsic, intrinsic, or blocked stealth state applies and this is not initial donning. Cloak_on() returns 0; both source callers discard that result.
callers: do_wear.c:2209-2428 accessory_or_armor_on() sets ga.afternmv=Cloak_on after setworn() when obj==uarmc (2388-2389), then calls unmul() immediately for zero-delay cloaks (2395-2402). do_wear.c:2432-2450 dowear() and :2454-2469 doputon() dispatch selected items into this helper.
hack.c:4177-4207 unmul() clears and invokes ga.afternmv, explicitly discarding its int result (4200-4206); JavaScript production path is js/hack.js unmul() invoking state.afternmv.

do_wear.c:1537-1568 set_wear() directly calls Cloak_on() for an already-worn startup or transformed cloak (1557-1558); allmain.c:73 invokes startup set_wear(). JavaScript production path is js/moveloop_preamble.js -> js/do_wear.js set_wear().

The assigned user command is wired through js/cmd.js W -> js/do_wear.js dowear() -> accessory_or_armor_on(); js/do_wear.js also wires P -> doputon() -> the same helper. Its current cloakOnPorted() guard rejects ELVEN_CLOAK before setworn(), while its partial Cloak_on() has no ELVEN_CLOAK case.
dependencies: do_wear.c:107-145 toggle_stealth(obj, oldprop, TRUE) is the direct same-file dependency for ELVEN_CLOAK. Its return is void and nothing consumes a return value, but its source effects are required by this case: when the stealth checks pass it calls makeknown() and emits “You move very quietly.”; oldprop is the STEALTH extrinsic with WORN_CLOAK removed, and the helper also reads HStealth, BStealth, and gi.initial_don.

The cloak slot and property state are written before the callback: accessory_or_armor_on() calls setworn(obj, mask) at do_wear.c:2376, and Cloak_on() reads uarmc->otyp, objects[otyp].oc_oprop, and u.uprops[oc_oprop].extrinsic. Cloak_on() and unmul()/set_wear() return values are discarded by their callers.

The rest of the complete Cloak_on() body has branch-local calls/state effects that remain in its whole-function scope: toggle_displacement() for CLOAK_OF_DISPLACEMENT; makeknown() for protection/invisibility cases; newsym() and visibility/invisibility state for mummy wrapping and cloak of invisibility; Tobjnam()/pline() for oilskin; EAcid_resistance for the alchemy smock; and update_inventory() after marking an unknown cloak. These branches are not the assigned case’s first mismatch.

evidence: Saved diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-enchants-high-elven-armor.json is for this exact v15 case and reports screensEmitted=30, stop at zero-based step 30, key “o”, with refusal “unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: wear reached an unported branch: Cloak_on() for otyp 139”. Its stop context is after #wizwish +6 elven cloak, takeoff of the prior cloak, and the W wear command.

The immutable C recording challenges/cases/v15/wizard-enchants-high-elven-armor.session.json has 77 steps. At zero-based step 30, selecting the elven cloak produces “You move very quietly.  You are now wearing an elven cloak.” C source do_wear.c:325-379 owns the callback: its ELVEN_CLOAK case calls toggle_stealth() at 341-343, then marks an unknown cloak known and updates inventory at 375-378. The JavaScript guard in js/do_wear.js:3459-3465 rejects this otyp before setworn(), so the queue annotation naming Cloak_on() is consistent with the first missing C behavior.

C source do_wear.c:2388-2402 establishes runtime reachability from dowear()/doputon() through accessory_or_armor_on(), and hack.c:4200-4206 invokes the deferred callback while discarding its return. do_wear.c:1557-1558 and allmain.c:73 establish the independent startup set_wear() caller.

Keep the later read path separate: the same C recording reaches step 75 with rn2(6)=5 at read.c:1179 and step 76 reports that the +6 elven cloak “violently glows silver for a while, then evaporates.” read.c:1164-1189 owns that enchant-armor threshold behavior; it is downstream of the do_wear.c first mismatch and is not part of this investigation’s source scope.
